title: Mom's busy Saturday
setting: A weekday evening. Yuki phones her mother to ask her out on Saturday, sure that she'll be free.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: moshimoshi, okaasan? ne, doyoubi, dokka asobi ni ikanai?
lines.ja: もしもし、お母さん？ね、土曜日、どっか遊びに行かない？
lines.kana: もしもし、おかあさん？ね、どようび、どっかあそびにいかない？
lines.english: Hi, Mom? Hey, do you want to go out somewhere on Saturday?

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: doyoubi? doyoubi wa ne, chotto isogashii no.
lines.ja: 土曜日？土曜日はね、ちょっと忙しいの。
lines.kana: どようび？どようびはね、ちょっといそがしいの。
lines.english: Saturday? Saturday I'm a bit busy, actually.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: e, nande? dokka asobi ni iku no?
lines.ja: え、なんで？どっか遊びに行くの？
lines.kana: え、なんで？どっかあそびにいくの？
lines.english: Huh, how come? Are you going out somewhere?

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: juuji kara, satou-san to sanpo ni iku no.
lines.ja: 10時から、佐藤さんと散歩に行くの。
lines.kana: じゅうじから、さとうさんとさんぽにいくの。
lines.english: At ten I'm going for a walk with Satou-san.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.ja: 散歩に行くだけでしょ？
lines.kana: さんぽにいくだけでしょ？
lines.english: That's just a walk, though, right?

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: uun. de, niji kara wa, tomodachi to eiga ni iku no.
lines.ja: ううん。で、2時からは、友達と映画に行くの。
lines.kana: ううん。で、にじからは、ともだちとえいがにいくの。
lines.english: Nope. Then at two, I'm going to the movies with a friend.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: eiga iku no? ii naa. watashi, doyoubi wa uchi de eiga miru dake da yo.
lines.ja: 映画行くの？いいなあ。私、土曜日はうちで映画見るだけだよ。
lines.kana: えいがいくの？いいなあ。わたし、どようびはうちでえいがみるだけだよ。
lines.english: You're going to the movies? Lucky you. All I'm doing on Saturday is watching a movie at home.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: eiga ni itte, shichiji kara wa minna de karaoke ni iku no.
lines.ja: 映画に行って、7時からはみんなでカラオケに行くの。
lines.kana: えいがにいって、しちじからはみんなでからおけにいくの。
lines.english: After the movie, at seven we're all going to karaoke.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: honto ni? okaasan ga karaoke iku no?
lines.ja: ほんとに？お母さんがカラオケ行くの？
lines.kana: ほんとに？おかあさんがからおけいくの？

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: iku yo. uta o utau no, kimochi ii n da kara.
lines.ja: 行くよ。歌を歌うの、気持ちいいんだから。
lines.kana: いくよ。うたをうたうの、きもちいいんだから。
lines.english: Of course I do. Singing feels great, you know.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.ja: お母さん、私より忙しいね。
lines.kana: おかあさん、わたしよりいそがしいね。
lines.english: Mom, you're busier than I am.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.ja: じゃあ、ユキもカラオケ行く？
lines.kana: じゃあ、ゆきもからおけいく？
lines.english: Well then, do you want to come to karaoke too?

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.kana: いくいく！じゃあ、しちじね。

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: de, nichiyoubi wa hima da kara, yuki no uchi ni asobi ni iku ne.
lines.ja: で、日曜日は暇だから、ユキのうちに遊びに行くね。
lines.kana: で、にちようびはひまだから、ゆきのうちにあそびにいくね。
lines.english: And Sunday I'm free, so I'll come over to your place.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: uchi ni? ii kedo, nani suru no?
lines.ja: うちに？いいけど、何するの？
lines.kana: うちに？いいけど、なにするの？
lines.english: My place? Sure, but what do you want to do?

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: yuki to sanpo ni iku no. hachiji ni iku kara ne!
lines.ja: ユキと散歩に行くの。8時に行くからね！
lines.kana: ゆきとさんぽにいくの。はちじにいくからね！
lines.english: We'll go for a walk together. I'll be there at eight!

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: hachiji!? watashi no nichiyoubi mo, isogashiku natchatta.
lines.ja: 8時！？私の日曜日も、忙しくなっちゃった。
lines.kana: はちじ！？わたしのにちようびも、いそがしくなっちゃった。
lines.english: Eight?! Now my Sunday's busy too.

questions.english: What happens in this phone call?

choices.english: Her mother is busy all Saturday, so Yuki stays in with a movie, and her mother will visit her on Sunday instead.
Yuki plans a Saturday of movies and karaoke for her mother, and on Sunday they'll both go walking with Satou-san.
Yuki asks her mother out, finds her Saturday is packed, joins her at karaoke, and gets booked for a Sunday walk.

questions.explanation: Line 1: Yuki asks her mother out (dokka asobi ni ikanai?). Lines 2-8: her mother's Saturday is full: a walk with Satou-san at ten, a movie with a friend at two, karaoke with everyone at seven. Lines 12-13: her mother asks Yuki to come to karaoke, and Yuki says iku iku. Lines 14-16: on Sunday her mother will come over to Yuki's place and take her for a walk at eight, so in line 17 Yuki's Sunday is busy too. A is wrong: watching a movie at home (line 7) was Yuki's plan before her mother asked her to karaoke, and in line 13 she says she'll come. B is wrong: the Saturday plans are her mother's own, not Yuki's. The walk with Satou-san is on Saturday at ten (line 4), and Sunday's walk is just Yuki and her mother (line 16).

questions.english: Kenta calls and asks, "nichiyoubi, uchi kuru? sora mo iru yo." (Want to come over on Sunday? Sora will be here too.) Say yes, you'll come over, using asobi ni iku.
questions.ja: 日曜日、うち来る？ソラもいるよ。
questions.kana: にちようび、うちくる？そらもいるよ。
questions.romaji: nichiyoubi, uchi kuru? sora mo iru yo.
questions.answer: Say you'll come over with asobi ni iku. Kenta asks with kuru, but you are the one going, so you answer with iku: un, asobi ni iku ne!

modelAnswers.romaji: iku iku! jaa, niji ni asobi ni iku yo.
modelAnswers.ja: 行く行く！じゃあ、2時に遊びに行くよ。
modelAnswers.english: I'm in! I'll come over at two, then.

questions.explanation: asobi ni iku is also the everyday way to say you'll visit someone's place. In line 14 Yuki's mother says yuki no uchi ni asobi ni iku ne (I'll come over to your place), and in line 16 hachiji ni iku kara ne (I'll be there at eight). Kenta says kuru because you'd be coming to him, but you answer from where you are, so it's iku. English 'I'll come over' tempts asobi ni kuru, but that would mean Kenta is the one coming. asobu on its own (asobu yo) sounds like kids playing. Adults say asobi ni iku. iku iku is the eager yes Yuki gives in line 13.

questions.english: Yuki's mother says, "niji kara wa, tomodachi to eiga ni iku no." What is she doing at two?
questions.ja: お母さんは2時から何をしますか？
questions.kana: おかあさんはにじからなにをしますか？
questions.romaji: okaasan wa niji kara nani o shimasu ka?

choices.english: Going out to the cinema with a friend.
Watching a movie at home with a friend.
Going over to a friend's place to watch a movie there.

questions.explanation: eiga ni iku is going out to see a film, at the cinema. Yuki takes it that way: eiga iku no? ii naa (line 7, You're going to the movies? Lucky you). In line 8 her mother goes straight on from the film to karaoke (eiga ni itte, then karaoke at seven). B is wrong: watching a film at home is eiga o miru, and that's Yuki's Saturday, not her mother's (line 7: uchi de eiga miru dake). C would be tomodachi no uchi de eiga o miru. eiga ni iku means the cinema, not a friend's place.

questions.english: You're putting your shoes on at the door, and Okaasan asks, "are, doko iku no?" (Oh, where are you off to?) Tell her you're just popping out for a walk.
questions.answer: Say you're going for a walk with sanpo ni iku. The everyday line on the way out is chotto sanpo ni itte kuru (I'm popping out for a walk, back soon).

modelAnswers.ja: ちょっと散歩行ってくるね。
modelAnswers.english: Just popping out for a walk.

modelAnswers.romaji: tenki ii kara, chotto sanpo ni itte kuru.
modelAnswers.ja: 天気いいから、ちょっと散歩に行ってくる。
modelAnswers.english: It's nice out, so I'm going for a quick walk.

questions.explanation: sanpo is the walk, and you go on one: sanpo ni iku, as Yuki's mother says in line 4 (satou-san to sanpo ni iku no) and line 16 (yuki to sanpo ni iku no). Not sanpo o toru, copied from 'take a walk'. itte kuru (go and come back) is what you say on your way out the door, and casual speech often drops ni (sanpo itte kuru). The second model adds tenki ii (it's nice out), from an earlier chunk.

questions.english: Yuki's mother tells Yuki her plan for seven o'clock. What did she say?
questions.ja: お母さんは何と言いましたか？
questions.kana: おかあさんはなんといいましたか？
questions.romaji: okaasan wa nan to iimashita ka?

choices.english: At seven we're all singing karaoke.
choices.romaji: shichiji kara wa minna de karaoke o utau no.

choices.english: At seven we're all going to karaoke.
choices.romaji: shichiji kara wa minna de karaoke ni iku no.

choices.english: At seven we're all going out.
choices.romaji: shichiji kara wa minna de asobi ni iku no.

questions.explanation: Line 8: shichiji kara wa minna de karaoke ni iku no. Karaoke is a place you go, so the noun goes straight before ni iku. Yuki echoes it in line 9 with ni dropped (okaasan ga karaoke iku no?), and her mother uses the same shape to invite her in line 12 (yuki mo karaoke iku?). A is 'sing karaoke' copied from English: karaoke o utau sounds off to many speakers. What you sing is uta, songs, which is how her mother puts it in line 10 (uta o utau no, kimochi ii n da kara). C is good Japanese for a night out, but it doesn't say where. Her mother names karaoke, and that's why Yuki is so surprised in line 9.

newWords.english: somewhere (casual for dokoka; dokka asobi ni ikanai? = want to go out somewhere?)
just, only (eiga miru dake = just watching a movie)
than (watashi yori isogashii = busier than me)
